# Results: synthetic CTR model (2026-11-11)

**All numbers are from synthetic worlds** generated by the ad-format fork (`synthetic/FORK_SPEC.md`).
They describe the pipeline on generated data and claim nothing about real traffic (rule R1).

## Setup

- Worlds: default (gamma = 1.0) and the negative control (gamma = 0), seeds 0, 1, 2 each; 50,000 users,
  40 campaigns, 28 days, target CTR 1%. About 2.6 million served impressions and 26,000 clicks per world.
- Each model is trained on seed 0's train days (0-20, about 2.0 million impressions), calibrated on its
  validation days (21-23) and evaluated on the test days (24-27) of seed 0 and of the unseen worlds 1 and 2.
  Seeds 1 and 2 have different users, campaigns and campaign quality, so they test transfer to a world the
  model never saw.
- Metrics on observed clicks: AUC, log loss (base rate = predicting the test CTR), expected calibration
  error over 20 equal-mass bins. Against the truth (`evaluation/ctr_truth.py`): mean absolute gap to the
  true click probability, correlation with it, and the share of the oracle's log-loss gain over the base
  rate that the model recovers.

## Default world (gamma = 1.0), test days

| World | Model | AUC | Log loss (base rate) | ECE | Mean pred / CTR | Gap to truth | Corr. with truth | Oracle gain recovered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| s0 (train world) | LogReg | 0.652 | 0.05542 (0.05699) | 0.0008 | 0.01064 / 0.01022 | 0.0068 | 0.49 | 31% |
| s0 (train world) | CADET | **0.670** | **0.05506** | 0.0008 | 0.01040 / 0.01022 | **0.0065** | **0.52** | **37%** |
| s1 (unseen) | LogReg | 0.600 | 0.05696 (0.05734) | 0.0024 | 0.01164 / 0.01029 | 0.0076 | 0.34 | 10% |
| s1 (unseen) | CADET | **0.627** | **0.05638** | 0.0019 | 0.01181 / 0.01029 | **0.0073** | **0.42** | 22% |
| s2 (unseen) | LogReg | 0.608 | 0.05662 (0.05718) | 0.0022 | 0.01215 / 0.01026 | 0.0078 | 0.36 | 12% |
| s2 (unseen) | CADET | **0.641** | **0.05595** | 0.0013 | 0.01132 / 0.01026 | **0.0071** | **0.43** | 25% |

CADET is better than the baseline on every world and every metric except calibration in the large on s1.

Per format on s0 (CADET AUC / ECE): banner 0.657 / 0.0008, interstitial 0.657 / 0.0013, rewarded
0.597 / 0.0012. Rewarded is hardest by construction: the fork halves the affinity term there (F3).

## Negative control (gamma = 0), test days

| World | Model | AUC | Log loss (base rate) | ECE | Corr. with truth | Oracle gain recovered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| s0 | LogReg | 0.635 | 0.05512 (0.05627) | 0.0009 | 0.56 | 32% |
| s0 | CADET | 0.648 | 0.05486 | 0.0003 | 0.62 | 42% |
| s1 | CADET | 0.616 | 0.05589 (0.05674) | 0.0015 | 0.50 | 24% |
| s2 | CADET | 0.622 | 0.05546 (0.05638) | 0.0014 | 0.51 | 27% |

With gamma = 0 the planted personal affinity is gone, but the click model still depends on page-context
match, ad format, fatigue and the attention state (absence is likelier at night), so a model still finds
signal; AUC is not expected to fall to 0.5. The gamma = 1 world adds 0.022 AUC on s0 (0.670 vs 0.648),
which is the part attributable to the planted personal signal.

## Findings that matter for serving

1. **Calibration holds on the training world but not across worlds.** On s0 the mean prediction is within
   2% of the CTR and ECE is 0.0008. On the unseen worlds the model over-predicts by 10-15% (s1: 0.01181
   vs 0.01029). Each world draws its own campaign creative quality and intercept, and the model has no
   campaign identity, so it cannot know a new world's level. Real traffic is a new world in this sense:
   the Platt scale fitted on synthetic validation data should not be expected to hold on real campaigns.
   This is the reason the server starts the model in shadow mode (admob_platform ADR 0004, resolution).
2. **Ranking survives the shift better than scale.** AUC drops from 0.670 to 0.63-0.64 on unseen worlds
   and stays above the baseline, so the order of candidates within a request transfers better than the
   absolute probability.
3. **The model is small enough for the budget.** NFR-33 allows 50 ms p99 for one scoring call.

## Latency (NFR-33: p99 <= 50 ms, all candidates of one request in one call)

ONNX Runtime 1.31, CPU, one intra-op thread, 32 history events.

| Candidates | CADET p50 / p99, PC (Python) | CADET p50 / p99, serving host (Go, incl. feature build) | LogReg p99, serving host |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.33 / 0.55 ms | 0.39 / 0.79 ms | 0.22 ms |
| 10 | 0.42 / 0.71 ms | 0.50 / 0.79 ms | 0.34 ms |
| 40 | 0.61 / 1.34 ms | 0.74 / 2.01 ms | 0.48 ms |
| 100 | 1.10 / 2.27 ms | 1.23 / 1.95 ms | 0.82 ms |

The serving host is the production node (AMD EPYC 9354P, 4 vCPU), measured with
`services/ad-serving/internal/pctr/latency_test.go`. The production histogram
`ad_serving_pctr_scoring_seconds` records the same call under live load.
